The Internal Linking Doesn't Show The Relative Importance Of The Content.

01

THERE ARE INTERNAL REDIRECTS THAT AREN'T 301.

MEDIUMFile Attachment

If you need to change the URL of a page as it is shown in search engine results, we recommend that you use a server-side 301 redirect. This is the best way to ensure that users and search engines are directed to the correct page.

The 301-status code means that a page has permanently moved to a new location. We have identified that some redirects are using 3XX redirects’

Findings & evidence
Both internal redirects on www return 302 (temporary), not 301, and both hand the visitor to a different host:
• /CriticalIllness/step_1 → 302 → ft.tipinsure.com/CriticalIllness/step_1
• /NewsAndActivities/index_v4/… → 302 → ft.tipinsure.com/NewsAndActivities/index_v4/…

Across the wider crawl the split is 1,202 redirects returning 301 and 94 returning 302. 61 of those 94 are on www, and every internal redirect found on www is a 302 — all of them article URLs being handed to ft.
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Change 302 redirects to 301 redirects
02

THERE ARE INTERNAL JAVASCRIPT REDIRECTS.

MEDIUMFile Attachment

If you need to change the URL of a page as it is shown in search engine results, we recommend that you use a server-side 301 redirect. This is the best way to ensure that users and search engines are directed to the correct page.

The 301-status code means that a page has permanently moved to a new location. We have identified that some redirects are using JavaScript redirects

Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations

THERE ARE INTERNAL REDIRECT CHAINS/CANONICAL CHAINS

MEDIUM

When using redirects to indicate moved URLs, or canonical tags for duplicate content, they should not be chained through multiple URLs, and should link direct to the final destination URLs 

Fix chained redirect - 301 redirect in 1 hop

Currently, we have noticed chained redirect from HTTP to preferred HTTPS version (https://www.example.com/bank/th/home.html).

We recommend 301 redirecting from all versions to the preferred version in 1 hop.

Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Implement 301 redirect from:

1. http://tipinsure.com

2. http://www.tipinsure.com         301 redirect in 1 hop to      https://www.tipinsure.com 

3. https://tipinsure.com

The Site Is Slow Enough That Google May Prefer Not To Show It To Searchers.

04

IMAGES ARE OVERLY LARGE

HIGHFile Attachment

Page speed matters to users and to search engines, and large images are the most common reason a page is slow to load. Every kilobyte beyond what the layout actually displays is downloaded, paid for by the visitor's connection, and then discarded by the browser.

Images should be compressed, saved in a modern format, and scaled to the size they are displayed at.

Findings & evidence
43 images exceed 300 kB, totalling 28.2 MB between them. A further 82 sit between 100 kB and 300 kB.

Heaviest:
• www5.dhipaya.co.th/TIPINSURE//files/tip_smart_premium/banner.jpg — 2.53 MB, 1440×3733
• www.tipinsure.com/assets/images/ta/th-color.svg — 1.49 MB, 1571×927
• www5.dhipaya.co.th/TIPINSURE/banner/promotion_content/thumb2026… — 1.46 MB, 3333×1042
• ft.tipinsure.com/files/banner/landing/condo_2017/landing_page.jpg — 1.39 MB, 1280×2500
• www5.dhipaya.co.th/TIPINSURE/imgs/product_details/pet/pet-asset-2.svg — 1.36 MB, 1143×643

Most widely used: a 1.04 MB news thumbnail at 2481×3509 is loaded on 51 pages, and the 1.36 MB pet SVG on 34 pages.

Where they live: 35 of the 43 are served from www5.dhipaya.co.th, 4 from ft.tipinsure.com, 2 from www.tipinsure.com and 2 from tipsnack.tipinsure.com.

Several are far larger than their display size — a 2481×3509 image used as a thumbnail, and a 3333×1042 banner — so the excess weight is downloaded and then discarded by the browser. The homepage scores 33 on PageSpeed Insights for mobile with a failing Core Web Vitals assessment, and image payload is the largest single contributor.
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Compress every image over 300 kB, and set 300 kB as the ceiling for new uploads.
  • Resize images to the dimensions they are actually displayed at before uploading — several are several times larger than their rendered size.
  • Serve modern formats (WebP or AVIF) with a JPEG or PNG fallback.
  • Add width and height attributes so the browser can reserve space and avoid layout shift.
  • Sample of Plugin and Compressor Website
  • https://shortpixel.com/ (Compression Website)
  • https://squoosh.app/ (Compression Website)
  • https://img-resize.com/ (Compression Website)

Duplication Could Be Causing Google To Ignore Pages

05

THERE ARE MULTIPLE OF HOMEPAGE DUPLICATION

HIGHFile Attachment

Homepage Duplication Found:

  • https://www.tipinsure.com/ (Main version)
  • https://tipinsure.com/
Findings & evidence
https://www.tipinsure.com/ and https://tipinsure.com/ both return 200 and are byte-identical — 222,442 bytes, matching MD5 hash. There is no host redirect between them and no canonical tag on either. A third variant, https://www.tipinsure.com with no trailing slash, serves the same content again.

robots.txt and sitemap.xml both declare the www host. The crawl found 2,411 exact-duplicate pages across the estate, 29 of them on www.
Our recommendations
  • Choose Preferred Version: Determine which version of the homepage URL is the primary and preferred one

(e.g., https://www.tipinsure.com/).

  • 301 Redirects: Implement 301 redirects from all duplicate homepage URLs to the preferred version. For example, https://tipinsure.com/ should all 301 redirect to https://www.tipinsure.com/
  • Canonical Tag (Optional): On the non-preferred duplicate pages, you can add a canonical tag in the <head> section pointing to the preferred URL. However, 301 redirects are generally preferred over canonical tags for homepage duplication.
  • Update Internal Links: Ensure all internal links on the website point to the preferred homepage URL.
  • Submit Sitemap: Submit an updated sitemap to Google Search Console with only the preferred homepage URL.

XML SITEMAPS AREN'T UPLOADED TO GSC.

HIGH

Google Search console is a dashboard from Google that helps you manage & troubleshoot your web site in Google’s index. Your sites’ XML sitemap should be submitted in Search Console to help with content discovery.

It appears that “Sitemap” on Search Console is currently uploaded but it has only 13 pages .

Findings & evidence
No sitemap submission could be confirmed for the property. sitemap.xml itself is reachable at https://www.tipinsure.com/sitemap.xml and is correctly declared in robots.txt, so the file is not the problem — what cannot be verified from a crawl is whether it has been submitted to, and is being read by, Search Console.
Our recommendations
  • Set up Google Search Console for the website
  • Submit XML sitemaps to Search Console

PAGES / URLS NOT INCLUDED IN SITEMAP.XML

HIGHFile Attachment

Ensure all important, indexable pages are included in your sitemap. Regularly audit your website and sitemap to identify and add any missing pages.

Submit your sitemap to search engine consoles like Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. For dynamically generated content or large websites.

Example of URLs not included in sitemap.xml:

Findings & evidence
sitemap.xml lists 13 URLs. The audit found 34 live pages on www, and the crawl found 11,161 crawled URLs that appear in no sitemap.

Absent from the sitemap: all 12 /Promotions/content/ pages, the three /tourist/ta_step_1/ quote pages, the three /health/step_1/ quote pages, and all four Thai-keyword landing URLs. Two of the 13 URLs it does list — /tourist/product_detail/domestic and /tourist/product_detail/inbound — return 404.

08

PAGINATED PAGES CANNOT BE CRAWLED.

HIGH

To ensure search engines can discover, crawl and index all pages, links to paginated pages must be implemented in such a way that they can be crawled by search engines. Infinite scroll (also referred to as “lazy loading) to load new content.

The article listings are not on www. /NewsAndActivities/ returns a 302 to ft.tipinsure.com, and ft's robots.txt disallows /NewsAndActivities/index_v2 and /NewsAndActivities/index_v3 — the paginated listing paths. 8,134 URLs on ft are blocked by robots.txt as a result.

The crawl also found 51 pages carrying links that are not <a href> elements, so they cannot be followed at all. Individual articles therefore have no crawlable discovery path.
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.

That means the web page, in this case the home page, does not load additional content until a visitor scrolls to the bottom of the screen. What Googlebot does is land on a page and crawl what is immediately visible.

Googlebot not being able to scroll could potentially lead to a lot of content missing from Google’s search index. We recommend changing to pagination.

Pagination helps your visitor and Google to ‘jump’ through your archive and find specific items they are looking for.

Findings & evidence
the news and article archive is not on www at all. /NewsAndActivities/ 302s to ft.tipinsure.com, and ft's robots.txt disallows /NewsAndActivities/index_v2 and /NewsAndActivities/index_v3 — the paginated listing paths.
Consequence: paginated article listings cannot be crawled, so individual articles have no crawlable discovery path. The Screaming Frog crawl 16 Sep 2026 (whole tipinsure.com estate) confirms this: 8,134 ft URLs blocked by robots.txt.
Our recommendations
  • Change from using “Load More” to Pagination
  • Canonicalize all pagination pages as “self-referencing”
  • Implement Google’s best practices so paginated pages can be crawled:

https://developers.google.com/search/docs/guides/lazy-loading?hl=en#paginated-infinite-scroll

https://developers.google.com/search/docs/guides/lazy-loading?hl=en

09

ROBOTS.TXT BLOCKS CONTENT WE WANT IN THE INDEX.

HIGH

A Robots.txt file can be used to control crawling where you have pages that you do not want to be crawled by Search Engines. We have identified there are pages that are being blocked from being crawled by Google via the robots .txt file, but these are valid pages we want indexed.

Findings & evidence
Two separate robots.txt files are involved.

On www.tipinsure.com: Disallow: /pa/ blocks the entire personal accident section, not only its checkout steps. The remaining rules — /api/, /payment/ and the motor, tourist and health step_2 to step_4 paths — are correct.

On ft.tipinsure.com: the article listing paths are disallowed, and every rule is addressed to User-agent: Googlebot plus two misspelled variants, "Googlebot-Moblie" and "Googlebot Smartphone". There is no User-agent: * block at all, so Googlebot is the one crawler being restricted while every other crawler is unrestricted.

Across the crawl, 10,380 URLs were blocked by robots.txt.
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Remove Disallow: /pa/ so the personal accident section can be crawled, and disallow only its checkout steps (/pa/step_2, /pa/step_3, /pa/step_4).
  • On ft.tipinsure.com, unblock /NewsAndActivities/index_v2 and index_v3 so the article listings can be crawled, and rewrite the rules against User-agent: * rather than Googlebot alone.
  • Replace the current robots.txt file with the amended one provided, so it appears at the following URL:

https://tipinsure.com/robots.txt

CREATE LANGUAGE PATH FOR EACH LANGUAGE AND LINK TO EQUIVALENT PAGE ON LANGUAGE SWITCHING MENU

MEDIUM

Currently, the site has 2 languages, ENG and THAI, but they are using the same URL for both languages by embedding the document location in <html>.

Findings & evidence
The site is Thai-only. Every page carries <html lang="th-TH">. /en returns 404 and /en/ returns 308. No language switcher appears in the markup, and no /en/ or other language path exists.

Locale is instead expressed as a query parameter: https://www.tipinsure.com/?lang=en returns 200 and serves a full page.
Our recommendations
  • Use language path to indicate each language separately in subdirectories
  • Link out from switching menu directly without having any redirect

For example: Home page

ENG: https://www.tipinsure.com/en/ showing ENG content 

THAI: https://www.tipinsure.com/ showing THAI content 

For example: Other pages  

ENG: https://www.tipinsure.com/en/motor/ showing ENG content 

THAI: https://www.tipinsure.com/motor/ showing THAI content 

11

INTERNAL LINKING IS NOT FULLY OPTIMIZED

HIGH

Effective internal linking strategies are vital for both user experience and SEO. Key optimization techniques include using descriptive anchor text, embedding contextual links, deep linking, prioritizing link quality over quantity..

For structuring, consider a hierarchical model, silo structure for thematic grouping. This process requires continuous review and adjustment.

Findings & evidence
Internal linking is the weakest structural signal on the site.
• the homepage exposes only 11 real internal page links in the raw HTML
• 16 of the 34 live www pages cannot be reached from the homepage by following links, including all 12 /Promotions/content/ pages
• the whole reachable site is 2 clicks deep, so there is no topical hierarchy to read
• the crawl found 2,425 pages with no internal outlinks at all, and 8,747 pages whose links appear only after JavaScript runs
Our recommendations
  • Anchor Text: Use descriptive, relevant, and varied anchor text, incorporating keywords naturally.
  • Contextual Linking: Embed links within content for added context, ensuring relevance and natural flow.
  • Primal will provide internal links URL for SEO target pages
12

ERROR PAGES DO NOT RETURN A 404 STATUS CODE OR SOFT 404

MEDIUM

When a page no longer exists, it should return a 404 status. Returning a success code, or redirecting the URL can result in error pages becoming indexed and Google crawling none existing URLs. 

For example: 

Non-exisitng URL is currently show 200 status code

Findings & evidence
Error handling is inconsistent across the site.
• Correct: /motor/motor_step_1/zzz-nope and /product_detail/health/zzz-nope both return a clean 404.
• Incorrect: /NewsAndActivities/index_v4/zzz-nope returns 302, is passed to ft.tipinsure.com, and ends at ft.tipinsure.com/Error/pageNotFound, which returns 200 OK.

Google reads a 200 as a live page, so every mistyped or retired article URL becomes a soft 404 in the index.

The 404 page that is served carries only the site shell and navigation — no "page not found" message, no search, no suggested links.
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Change redirect method to direct to an error 404 page
  • Create 404 custom page
  • It should go to a custom 404 page as the following example below, not to the home page and return 404 status code

INTERNAL LINKS POINT TO URL RETURNING 4XX STATUS CODES OR NO RESPONSE

HIGHFile Attachment

Although broken pages themselves are not an issue, you should no longer link to pages if they have been removed. If there are many 4XX Status Code such as 404 (Broken Links) within a site, it can be a signal to Google of low quality, non-maintained site.

Therefore, we strongly recommend fixing any links that point to broken URLs sending a status code to 404 (Not Found).

Findings & evidence
27 internal URLs return 404, and they are linked from 22,061 places across the estate.

Ranked by inlinks:
• /Home/cookie_privacy — 17,485 inlinks. This is the cookie-notice link in the shared footer, so it is broken on effectively every page.
• /motor/motor_step_1/ompulsory — 1,106 inlinks. A typo: the leading "c" of "compulsory" is missing.
• /Motor/motor_step_1/compulsory, /Motor/motor_step_1/3 and /Motor/motor_step_1/3_plus — 998 inlinks each.
• /Health/index 87 · /Tourist/ta_step_1/domestic 59 · /Tourist/ta_step_1/inbound 42 · /Health/product_choose 34 · /files/privacy_policy/personal_data_privacy_2026.pdf 19 · /Promotions/index/14 17 · /Health/step_1 17 · /Motor/motor_product_detail/first_class_lady 17

The pattern: capitalised path variants return 404 while the lowercase equivalents return 200, so routing is case-sensitive and something on the site still emits the capitalised form.

Where the links come from: 21,867 of the 22,061 are on ft.tipinsure.com and 92 are on www. The full source-page list is in the accompanying Affected URLs workbook, sheet "13b Pages linking to the 4xx URLs".
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Fix the broken link by replacing new resource
  • Implement 301 redirect from broken URL to relevant URL
  • If the destination page is deleted, cannot find a replacement for it or find at a new address, remove the broken link altogether.
  • If there is no correct link, consider removing the link from the page.
15

EXTERNAL LINKS

MEDIUMFile Attachment

When a website has hyperlinks pointing to 404 error pages on external sites, it can negatively impact SEO and user experience. These broken links can lead to higher bounce rates as visitors encounter dead ends, reducing trust and engagement on the site.

Search engines also see frequent 404s as a sign of poor site maintenance, which can affect rankings. Addressing these links promptly helps maintain SEO health, improves user flow, and ensures the site continues to provide reliable, high-quality resources.

Findings & evidence
Two separate problems on outbound links.

Broken external links. 59 external URLs return 4xx, linked from 24,336 places. All six of the heaviest are on the parent insurer's site and sit in the shared navigation:
• www.dhipaya.co.th/th/service-detail-6.html — 4,929 inlinks
• www.dhipaya.co.th/th/service-detail-11.html — 4,917 inlinks
• www.dhipaya.co.th/th/service-detail-2.html — 4,917 inlinks
• www.dhipaya.co.th/th/hospital — 3,817 inlinks
• www.dhipaya.co.th/th/repairer — 3,811 inlinks
• www.dhipaya.co.th/th/contact — 1,064 inlinks
On www alone these account for 201 links, all from the navigation, under anchors such as "ขั้นตอนการเคลม". The full source list is in the Affected URLs workbook.

Unsafe cross-origin links. 354 external links on www use target="_blank" without rel="noopener" or rel="noreferrer". Every page carries roughly ten, so this is template-level.
Note on ft.tipinsure.com. ft is the legacy front-end, due to be retired and replaced by www.tipinsure.com paths. Findings recorded against ft are listed so the behaviour is not carried over — they should be resolved on the destination www structure during migration rather than patched on ft.
Our recommendations
  • Remove or Replace Links, for each broken link, either remove it or replace it with a valid URL if there’s a similar resource available.
  • Use No-Follow Tags (Optional), for cases where the link is necessary but often unreliable, consider adding a rel="nofollow" to avoid SEO penalties.

ROBOTS.TXT ISN'T BLOCKING URLS/FOLDERS THAT WE DON'T WANT CRAWLED

HIGH

A Robots.txt file can be used to control crawling where you have pages that you do not want to be crawled by Search Engines. We have identified there are pages that should be excluded from being crawled by Google, such as the URLs below,

Findings & evidence
robots.txt blocks the checkout funnel and /api/, but nothing controls query parameters.

9,373 URLs in the crawl carry parameters — 49.8% of everything found. The patterns generating them:
• ?lang=en — returns a full 200 page, creating a duplicate of every page it is applied to
• ?gclid=, ?gad_source=, ?gbraid= — ad-tracking parameters that generate indexable duplicates of the motor quote pages
• /zhob/ — the tag-manager endpoint, crawled as if it were page content

None of these URLs carries a canonical tag, so nothing collapses them back to the original page. 35 internal links also carry Google Analytics utm or _ga parameters, which overwrite original session attribution when followed.
Our recommendations
  • Add parameter rules to robots.txt so tracking and locale parameters stop generating duplicate URLs.
  • Apply a self-referencing canonical on every page, which collapses the parameter variants that remain.
  • Remove Google Analytics utm and _ga parameters from internal links, so original session attribution is kept.

AI Accessibility & GEO Readiness

How well the site is prepared for AI crawlers, LLM answer engines and generative search.

1 Low 1 check

The Site Serves Too Many Unique Pages.

17

LLMS.TXT IS MISSING

LOWFile Attachment

The proposed llms.txt protocol, similar to robots.txt, allows content creators to guide how AI models access and use their content for training and response generation. It's not about "blocking" but "choosing" what content (URLs, summaries, or full text) is shown to AI platforms.

Why llms.txt Matters for SEO and GEO

  • Enable Content Analysis: A clean, flattened site enables AI-driven analysis like keyword frequency, taxonomy, entity, and competitive analysis.
  • Enhance AI Interaction: llms.txt helps LLMs efficiently retrieve accurate information.
  • Improve Content Visibility: Guides AI indexing, potentially boosting visibility in AI search (no guarantees, but a step forward).
  • Boost AI Performance: Ensures LLMs access valuable content, leading to accurate AI responses (chatbots, AI search). The "full" llms.txt rendering is preferred over summaries or URL lists.
  • Gain Competitive Advantage: Makes your site AI-ready as technology evolves.

24

URLS AREN'T SEARCH ENGINE FRIENDLY

MEDIUMFile Attachment

A URL is human-readable text that was designed to replace the numbers (IP addresses) that computers use to communicate with servers. They also identify the file structure on the given website. A URL consists of a protocol, domain name, and path.

Why do URLs matter for SEO?

  • Improved user experience

A well-crafted URL provides both humans and search engines an easy-to-understand indication of what the destination page will be about.

  • Rankings

URLs are a minor ranking factor; search engines use them when determining a particular page or resource's relevance to a search query.

  • Links

In a pinch, well-written URLs can serve as their own anchor text when copied and pasted as links in forums, blogs, social media networks, or other online venues. 

Point of Problems:

  • URLs Using Underscore/Uppercase

When necessary for readability, use hyphens or dash (-) to separate words. URLs should not use underscores, spaces, or any other characters to separate words.

Use lowercase letters. In some cases, uppercase letters can cause issues with duplicate pages.

For example:

https://www.tipinsure.com/tourist/ta_step_1/domestic


New URLs should look like this: https://www.tipinsure.com/tourist/ta-step-1/domestic

Change from: https://www.tipinsure.com/tourist/ta_step_1/domestic

To: https://www.tipinsure.com/tourist/ta-step-1/domestic


  • Non ASCIl Characters

We have noticed that currently some of the URLs in the site are named in other languages. As a result, this would make Google bots unable to predict what is inside of that content if URLs are named using Non ASCIl Characters

For example:

https://www.tipinsure.com/ประกันท่องเที่ยว


New URLs should look like this: https://www.tipinsure.com/travel-insurance

Change from: https://www.tipinsure.com/ประกันท่องเที่ยว

Findings & evidence
Three separate URL problems on www.

• Case sensitivity. Capitalised paths — /Motor/, /Health/, /Tourist/, /Home/, /Pm/ — return 404 while their lowercase equivalents return 200. 16 URLs are broken this way, and they are covered in full under the 4xx issue.
• Underscores. motor_step_1, ta_step_1 and product_choose all use underscores, which are weaker word separators than hyphens. 11,894 URLs in the crawl contain them.
• Non-ASCII. Four Thai-character URLs such as /ประกันรถยนต์ชั้น1 percent-encode into long unreadable strings when shared. 11,373 URLs in the crawl contain non-ASCII characters.

A further 12,150 URLs contain uppercase characters and 2,796 exceed 115 characters.
Our recommendations
  • Make sure visitor can understand what the page is all about by looking at URL
  • Use keyword in URL, avoid keyword repetition within URL
  • Do not include preposition or conjunction e.g. “and” or “the”
  • Use – (dashes) rather than _ (underscores) in a format that does not allow spaces
  • Apply Self-Referencing Canonical tag to New (Optimized) URLs
  • We highly recommend naming English URLs not Thai URLs if possible
  • Apply Pagination Canonical Tag to avoid a duplicate content problem
  • Parameter URLs change to static URLs
  • Select the preferrable version of URL (avoid duplicate content problem), so
    • the URL can be ending with a “Trailing Slash (/)”
  • Then 301 Redirect from Old URL > New URL
  • Primal will optimize for SEO target pages

THERE ARE DOORWAY PAGES

MEDIUMFile Attachment

Doorways are sites or pages created to rank highly for specific search queries. They are bad for users because they can lead to multiple similar pages in user search results, where each result ends up taking the user to essentially the same destination.

They can also lead users to intermediate pages that are not as useful as the final destination. We have identified that there are pages on the site that appear to be doorway pages e.g.

Findings & evidence
Four Thai-keyword URLs serve content identical to an existing funnel page, with no canonical tag between them:
• /ประกันรถยนต์ชั้น1 duplicates /motor/motor_step_1/first_class
• /ประกันการเดินทางต่างประเทศ, /ประกันท่องเที่ยว and /ประกันเดินทางต่างประเทศ all duplicate /tourist/ta_step_1/inter

Each pair is byte-identical and shares the same title, meta description and H1. A separate pair, /health/step_1/talisman and /health/step_1/tiphealthcare, serves one identical page for two different health products.

Keyword-named URLs that duplicate an existing page are the pattern Google describes as doorway pages.
Our recommendations
  • Consider removing the doorway pages we have discovered.
28

REMOVE META KEYWORDS

MEDIUMFile Attachment

We have noticed a lot of duplicate keywords being used in Meta Keyword on the website. Keyword stuffing refers to the practice of loading a webpage with keywords in an attempt to manipulate a site’s ranking in search results.

This attempt is aimed solely for the consumption of search engine crawlers and not actual ranking in response.

Findings & evidence
A meta keywords tag is present on every page — all 34 live www pages, and 11,172 across the wider crawl. It is in the shared layout rather than set per page.

The homepage value is:
<meta name="keywords" content="บริษัทประกันภัย,บริษัทประกันภัยรถยนต์, ประกันรถยนต์ออนไลน์, ผ่อนประกันรถยนต์.ประกันรถยนต์ผ่อนได้"/>

Note the malformed separator near the end — a full stop where a comma should be. Search engines have ignored this tag since 2009, and it publishes the keyword strategy to competitors on every page.
Our recommendations
  • Use only 1 unique keyword per page
  • OR remove all Meta keyword

THERE ARE UNNATURAL LINKS TOWARDS THE SITE.

HIGHFile Attachment

Spammy outgoing backlinks are links towards your website that have seemed to be low-quality, irrelevant, or manipulative. These links can negatively impact your site's SEO and user experience because they suggest your site is associated with untrustworthy sources or is attempting to manipulate search rankings rather than provide genuine value.

Search engines view these links as a sign of poor site quality, which can lead to lower rankings. We have identified that there are suspicious links to the site that appear to be low-quality, unnatural and spammy.

Findings & evidence
No backlink analysis was run as part of this onsite audit, so the inbound link profile has not been assessed. This check is recorded for completeness and needs referring-domain and anchor-text data from a backlink tool before it can be answered.
Our recommendations
  • Remove the unnatural links on the pages.
  • Disavow links on Google Search Console
30

CONTENT ON THE WEBSITE DID NOT FOLLOW E-E-A-T GUIDELINES

LOWFile Attachment

The new E-E-A-T acronym stands for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness. While E-E-A-T itself isn't a specific ranking factor, using a mix of factors that can identify content with good E-E-A-T is useful.

For example, our systems give even more weight to content that aligns with strong E-E-A-T for topics that could significantly impact the health, financial stability, or safety of people, or the welfare or well-being of society. We call these "Your Money or Your Life" topics, or YMYL for short.

Search quality raters are people who give us insights on if our algorithms seem to be providing good results, a way to help confirm our changes are working well. In particular, raters are trained to understand if content has strong E-E-A-T.

The criteria they use to do this is outlined in our search quality rater guidelines.

Our recommendations
  • Create Author Profile
    Findings & evidence — Author profile
    The editorial content carries no author attribution, no reviewer credentials and no publish or update dates in the markup. There is no Organization or Person schema anywhere on the site to establish who stands behind the advice, and company registration and licence details are not surfaced on the pages sampled.

    Insurance is a YMYL category, where Google and AI answer engines weight experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust signals heavily.

Having an author profile on the website would help with the “Authority” which helps the site to appear as credible from trusted writers who are an expert in the industry. Within the author profile, users would have an opportunity to explore written contents by the same author.

  • Add citation / sources in the content, especially YMYL content.

Adding citations from reliable sources would help the content in the website appear to have “Trustworthiness”

  • Add external links to trustworthy sources that are related to you niche naturally
  • Add FAQ Section on the product or service category page.
    • For e-commerce / service websites
    Findings & evidence — FAQ section
  • Optimize Google Business Profile for Local SEO
    Findings & evidence — Google Business Profile

Google Business Profile is a free feature from Google that helps business owners manage their online presence across the search engine and its growing portfolio of utilities, including Google Maps. Seasoned SEO professionals use Google Business Profiles to leverage a location-based strategy.

Creating a Google Business Profile is the first step to local search success.

  • Getting more positive reviews on Google maps
  • Add appealing images to show your business
  • Your profile information appears in several different areas of local search, including Google Maps.
  • Google Star ratings and reviews of your business will be visible in your profile.
  • You can create a strong first impression with the profile.
  • Used well, your profile can boost conversions too.
